title: Slow Coagulation Transscleral Cyclophotocoagulation for Postvitrectomy Patients With Silicone Oil–induced Glaucoma

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>); not CC BY, so the record is private

indication: medically uncontrolled secondary glaucoma after pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil injection (silicone oil in place throughout follow-up; open-angle, angle-closure and mixed mechanism); refractory
design: retrospective single-institution case series, 18 eyes of 18 patients with at least 1 year of follow-up

groups.description: slow-coagulation continuous-wave transscleral diode cyclophotocoagulation with the G-Probe (1250 mW, 4 s); repeat treatment allowed (titratable use)

series.notes: mean ± SD; N=18 per the Table 2 caption, per-visit n not reported; Table 2 'Retreatment (n)' row reports repeat TSCPC treatments around the 1- and 3-month visits, and those eyes stay in the means

exclusions.reason: changes duplicate the absolute IOP series of the same eyes
Kaplan-Meier estimates and success proportions are not admissible

exclusions.what: Table 2 medication and logMAR VA blocks; Table 3 complications

notes: Tonometer is not stated in the article; method unstated.
Preoperative IOP on glaucoma medication (medically uncontrolled; baseline medications tabulated in Table 2).
Repeat TSCPC was not counted as reoperation; one eye had GATT at 12 months as a glaucoma reoperation; no silicone oil removal during follow-up (Results).
Medication: mean number of glaucoma medications per visit is tabulated in Table 2; not extracted.
Exclusion of eyes with less than 1 year of follow-up is a completeness criterion, not outcome-defined.
